title: The Remonstrants keep the division of grace
source_text: XXI. Qui in Belgio Remonstrantes dicuntur, sive Arminiani, maxime probant & arcte retinent gratiae distinctionem in sufficientem atque efficacem, eamque putant multis scripturae locis subnixam, & necessariam plane ad justitiam divinam tuendam. Proinde negant gratiam sufficientem aliam non esse, quam quae est efficax, hoc est, quam quae actu ipso hominem conversum dat. Licet enim, inquiunt; maxima sit gratiae sufficientis ad operandum in homine conversionem efficacia & ἐνέργεια, tamen non semper illa, vitio nempe & culpa hominis, habet effectum, ipsumque conversionis ἀποτέλεσμα. Ut videre est in eorum Synodo in declaratione sententiae Remonstrantium circa tertium & quartum articulum pag. 15.
pass_a_gloss: XXI. Those who in the Low Countries are called Remonstrants, or Arminians, most strongly approve & firmly retain the distinction of grace into sufficient and efficacious, and think it supported by many places of scripture, & plainly necessary for upholding divine justice. Accordingly they deny that sufficient grace is none other, than that which is efficacious, that is, than that which in very act gives man converted. For although, they say; the efficacy & energeia of sufficient grace for working conversion in man be very great, yet it does not always, namely by the vice & fault of man, have its effect, and the very apotelesma of conversion. As may be seen in their Synod in the declaration of the opinion of the Remonstrants on the third & fourth article page 15.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXI. The Remonstrants of the Low Countries, also called Arminians, strongly approve the distinction of grace into sufficient and efficacious and hold firmly to it. They think it rests on many passages of Scripture and is plainly needed to defend God's justice.

So they deny that sufficient grace is only the grace that is efficacious, the grace that actually produces a converted person. 'Although,' they say, 'sufficient grace has the greatest efficacy and energy (energeia) for working conversion in a person, it does not always, through the person's own vice and fault, take effect and reach the actual outcome (apotelesma) of conversion.' This can be seen in their Synod, in the declaration of the Remonstrants' opinion on the third and fourth articles, page 15.
